Tune with your eyes closed: a tick for every kilohertz, a knock on a station.

Longwave is a valve radio for falling asleep. Its stations broadcast rain, sea, a night train and a stove, and spoken programmes built on ways to quiet the mind: a forecast for imaginary seas, a body roll call, a lottery of random words, 4-7-8 breathing, a slow inventory, a countdown. No account, no ads, no network: everything stays on your phone. Not a medical treatment.
Sounds: recordings from Freesound and SoundBible as edited for the Blanket project (CC0, CC BY, public domain). Voices: Silero and Kokoro neural voices. Fonts: Prata, PT Mono, Manrope, Caveat (OFL).
A valve radio for falling asleep
Turn the knob to find a station: rain over Rainford, the sea under a lighthouse, a night train, a stove.
Some stations talk, slowly and dull on purpose: a forecast for seas that aren\'t on any map, a body roll call, a lottery of random words, breathing to a metronome.
Pick when it goes off the air. At the end the station drifts away into the static, and the static goes quiet.
The morning after, the station sends a QSL card. Rare stations come on only some nights.
The app is made together with the people who use it. It all goes through the StillCraft bot on Telegram.
